v.description: The API version (`major.minor`): `tower api` prints it.
The API version (`major.minor`): `tower api` prints it.

BoardMsg.description: GET `/board` (SSE): the board, again whenever it changes, or why the tower can't build it until it can.

user.description: The person running the tower: `name` signs the notes renderers write for them (`user.name` in the config).

config.description: The config file's path: the system root, where the logs and collections are, is its directory.

keys.description: Every command's chords by id, the config's `keys` over the keymap's defaults (`/keymap.js`).

waiting.description: Who waits on you, in the order to go to them.

offers.description: Every floor's open offers, oldest first: a policy's slot waiting for someone to start it, until its next slot.
offers.deprecated: since 1.91: each floor's `x.policies.offers`, and its ask in `asks`, copied here until 2.0.

archiveAt.description: The latest change to any archived card (epoch ms; 0 with none archived): a renderer holding a floor's archive reads it again when this or the floor's `archived` moves.

rateLimitsAt.description: When the rate limits were read (epoch ms): a session's turn reads them, and the quota probe while no turn does, so they age only while neither reads.

rateLimitsFrom.description: Whose reading the rate limits are: a session's turn, or a probe's read.

turnLimits.description: The newest reading a session's turn took, beside the account's: what a probe of the limits waits on while turns read them.

reads.description: The probes the core ran before 1.90: their readers, a closed set.

every.description: How often it reads while nothing else holds it, ms.

lastAt.description: When it last read, answered or not.

error.description: Why its last read has no answer.

wait.description: How long it waits after its last read, ms: `every`, longer while backing off or unavailable.

nextAt.description: When it reads next: a moment past (0 before its first read) means at the tower's next tick.

held.description: `nextAt` is set by what the sessions read: a session's turn read every limit it reads, and it reads no sooner than `every` after.

probes.description: The quota probe, the quota extension's part (`x.quota`) as it stood at 1.89, with `run`, a read now (`probe/run`): none while the extension doesn't run.

extraUsage.description: The account's extra usage, as the probes' newest answer that had it said.

extensions.description: Every extension the tower found, bundled first, then by id, as it stands: started, or why not (decision `extensions`).

adds.description: What extensions' folds added to each subject, by its key (`card:<id>`, `floor:<project>`, `board`, `conversation:<id>`, `item.<collection>:<project>/<id>`, `<cap>.<kind>:<key>`), each tagged with its capability: `actionsOf` and `badgesOf` in `/cards.js` draw them beside the core's.

asks.description: What extensions' folds ask of the user, oldest first: in the attention order beside `waiting`.

x.description: Each extension's own part of the board, by capability, as its board fold made it.

today.description: Today so far, every project's: it moves with the facts the board moves with, so it is as of the last change.

hostOutdated.description: The running host speaks another protocol than its clients: it predates their code, until it is restarted.

claudeDefaults.description: The model and effort Claude starts a new worker on when asked for neither, as the sessions showed them.

claudeUntested.description: The releases outside the tested range that live workers run, each once.

process.description: The foreground process, such as `zsh` or `node`.

title.description: The terminal title the shell or its program set, if any.

Keys.description: Each command id with its chords, as written in a canonical form (`chordOf`).

cards.description: The cards of its present (`onBoard`); the rest are its archive, read at `GET /archive/<project>`.

archived.description: How many cards its archive holds.

threads.description: The review thread of each checkout that has one, their calls naming `review/append`.
threads.deprecated: since 1.93: the reviews extension's `x.reviews.threads`, copied here until 2.0.

main.description: Its main checkouts as git reads them, once every dir of it is read: what a checkout's state is read from (`src/bridge/checkouts.ts`).

policies.description: Its policies, in id order (decision `policies`), their calls naming `policy/*`.
policies.deprecated: since 1.91: the policies extension's `x.policies.policies`, copied here until 2.0.

gallery.description: The floor's last showings, any worker's, on duty or not, newest first (`galleryOf`).

git.description: Every dir of the floor reads as a git repo, so a checkout of it can be forked (`spawn`'s `cut.from`).

branchPrefix.description: What a cut's branch is named by default: this, then the worktree's name.

cutByDefault.description: Whether a new worker starts in a worktree of its own unless told where, when the floor can cut one.

hiring.description: How far its workers hire workers through `tower hire`.

tidy.description: What its Tidy would do now, as its call applies it.

x.description: Each extension's own part of it, by capability, as its floor fold made it.

color.description: A CSS color renderers mark the project's things with.

plugins.description: Absolute plugin directories this project's sessions load, beside the ones every session loads.

Floor.description: A project as a floor: its config, shelf included, its sessions' cards, its collections, and the tower's worktrees and kept branches in its repos. `bases`: the origin branches a cut can start from, the default first; empty when a dir isn't a git repo with an origin.

peer.description: The Claude session name its peers message it by (`SendMessage`'s `to`), while its Claude runs.

worktree.description: The worktree its cwd is, by name, the branch checked out there (none on a detached HEAD, or before git is read) and, for a fork, the checkout it was forked from; `gone` once git no longer lists it with its folder in every repo of the project (`checkoutGone`).

reviews.description: The callsign of the worker whose work this one reviews: the reviews extension's `x.reviews.of`, or for a reviewer spawned before reviews logged its facts, its first prompt (`legacyReviewer`).

hiredBy.description: The worker that hired this one (`tower hire`, `tower review`); a worker started any other way has none.

crew.description: The worker a launch contributor put this one in the crew of at its spawn (`tower.reports-to`), and the capability that did; a reviewer spawned before reviews logged its facts is in its author's, by reviews, as the board names the author now (`legacyCrew`).

exempt.description: What launch contributors exempted this worker from at its spawn (`tower.exempt`), each by its capability; a reviewer spawned before reviews logged its facts is exempt from hiring by reviews (`legacyReviewer`).

reportsTo.description: The card of the worker this one reports to, as it runs now (carried on through resumes): the worker of its `crew` edge, else its hirer. Only a worker's current card reports; nobody's when it reports to none.

checkout.description: The checkout it works in: its worktree's name, or `main`.

checkoutState.description: Where the work in its checkout stands: what its Changes are.

threadState.description: Where the work its review thread is about stands (`threadCheckoutOf`: a reviewer's is its author's), with the thread Tidy filed once it landed. The card offers `note` while it is live.
threadState.deprecated: since 1.93: the reviews extension's `x.reviews.threadState`, copied here until 2.0.

unseen.description: The messages of the review thread about its work (`threadCheckoutOf`: a reviewer's is its author's) it hasn't seen (after its own last one); none without a thread, or once `threadState` is no longer live.
unseen.deprecated: since 1.93: the reviews extension's `x.reviews.unseen`, copied here until 2.0.

blocked.description: The screen a `blocked` worker shows: answered on its terminal.

live.description: Its PTY is running: the screen is live and it takes keys.

waiting.description: Waiting on the user since `enteredAt`: held by a screen or a question, or an outcome nobody has typed to since, unless that outcome is an answer its running hirer is to read (`waitsOn`).

leaving.description: It runs and asked to go home (`tower home` with its own callsign) with no prompt since: once its turn completes, the tower runs its `send-home`. Its outcome waits on nobody; a screen or a question still waits on the user, since the turn can't end until someone answers it.

waitsOn.description: The worker whose prompt a hire's unread answer answers: its hirer as it runs now, while that runs.

typedAt.description: Epoch ms someone last typed into the session.

heardAt.description: Epoch ms Claude last raised a hook or a mod event.

stuck.description: Working with no word from Claude for `STUCK_MS`: a hung tool, or a long build.

broken.description: Its log holds an event the tower can't fold (`Facts.broken`): the error, the event's code and its time (epoch ms). Its facts stand as they were before it and are never folded on, so it waits on no one and is never stuck; whether it runs is the host's word, so it can still be driven and killed, or resumed once it no longer runs.

compacting.description: Claude is compacting the conversation, inside a turn or by `/compact`.

says.description: What Claude told the user between tool calls in the current turn, oldest first.

subagents.description: The subagents the session started, followed or not.

subagentRuns.description: The subagents the session started whose loops it follows, oldest first.

turns.description: The main loop's turns that ran to their Stop, across the sessions the worker ran as.

lineage.description: The sessions the worker ran as, oldest first, ending with this one.

claude.description: The release of Claude Code the session runs, once the mod reported it.

claudeUntested.description: Its Claude is outside the releases the tower is tested on (`CLAUDE_TESTED`).

resources.description: What the session left running, each with the verb that ends it alone.

shown.description: What the worker showed the user across the sessions it ran as, oldest first; `at` in epoch ms, `session` the one that showed it.

pages.description: The html files the worker wrote across the sessions it ran as, oldest first.

sent.description: The messages it sent other Claude sessions across the sessions it ran as, oldest first.

stranded.description: Ended while nobody meant it to end: the host stopped or died, or a signal from outside the tower killed it.

cutOff.description: Stranded mid-turn: it stopped or was lost while the main loop's turn ran (`isMidTurn`); a broken fold doesn't know where the turn stood. Its `carry-on` resumes it on a prompt telling Claude so (`CARRY_ON`).

letGoAt.description: When the user let it go, stranded (epoch ms): off duty, its conversation still resumable from the archive.

unresumable.description: Not running, holding a conversation nobody resumed, which can't be resumed where it ran: why.

conversations.description: The conversations Claude saved, in order: the last is the one a resume continues.

continuedBy.description: The session that carries this worker on, holding its callsign and showings from then on.

onDuty.description: Running, or stopped by the host or lost while its latest conversation waits to be resumed and can be, unless let go.

run.description: The run of a policy it is, through every resume: a run fact names the first session of its lineage.
run.deprecated: since 1.91: the policies extension's `x.policies.run`, copied here until 2.0.

seat.description: Where it sits on its floor, replayed from the floor's comings and goings (`withSeats`): every on-duty card has one.

actions.description: What can be done with it now, each verb with its call when it has one: `verbs` and `calls` say the same, apart.

x.description: Each extension's own part of it, by capability, as its card fold made it (decision `extensions`).

HiredBy.description: A hirer: the session it hired from, its callsign, and the floor it works on, which a hire on another floor doesn't share.

CrewEdge.description: A crew edge a launch contributor gave a spawn: the worker's callsign and session then, and `by`, its capability.

Exemption.description: An exemption a launch contributor gave a spawn: `from` the floor's hiring limits, `by` its capability.

filed.description: The thread Tidy filed once the work landed.
filed.deprecated: since 1.93: the reviews extension's `card.x.reviews.filed`, copied onto `card.checkoutState` until 2.0.

CheckoutState.description: Where a checkout's work stands. `live`: work can go on there. `landed`: its work is in its base, `on` naming that base while git still holds the worktree or a branch cut under its name, `empty` when git says no branch of it gained a commit since it was cut (there was nothing to land), `edited` how many of its commits landed as edited copies (carried) on `branch` (the landing read's). `gone`: its worktree is gone, and nothing says its work landed. The main checkouts are always live.

FiledThread.description: A thread Tidy filed: its item's id and tag, and when it was filed, as a message heading writes a time.

Status.description: `blocked`: held before it starts by one of Claude's screens (`blocked.ts`) until the user answers it. `watching`: the main loop's turn ended while something it started can start its next turn without the user (a background task, a `/loop`, a cron); `done`: it ended with nothing but the user to wake it. `failed`: the main loop's last turn ended in an API error or a refusal, with no answer to review.

BlockedKind.description: Claude's screens that hold a session before it starts: nothing happens until the user answers on the screen, and no hook is raised while they show. `trust`: the workspace trust dialog, raised in every folder Claude hasn't been told to trust (every new worktree). `login`: first-run setup and sign-in, raised when Claude has no account on this machine.

Attention.description: How loudly a worker asks for you, the one thing every renderer colours: the status word keeps the fact.

id.description: Claude's id for the subagent's loop; absent from a spawn the mod posted before it reported one, whose loop can't be followed.

description.description: The Agent call's few words on the task.

parent.description: The subagent whose loop spawned it; absent when the main loop did.

endedAt.description: When its loop last ended a turn, until it steps again.

ended.description: How that turn ended: `answer`, or `aborted` when it was stopped.

CardSubagent.description: A subagent the session started whose loop the tower follows (`SubagentRun` with an `id`), running while its loop is mid-turn in a live session.

Tokens.description: Tokens of one model step: fresh input, output, and the prompt cache read and written.

LineageSession.description: A session of a worker's lineage, and when it started (epoch ms).

CardResource.description: A process a session left running: `orphan` when re-parented to launchd.

ResourceVerb.description: A process a session left running can always be ended on its own.

items.description: The verb's input, the fields the board knows: `tower api <verb>` describes it.
The verb's input, the fields the board knows: `tower api <verb>` describes it.

ResourceAction.description: A verb offered now, with its call when it has one: `drive`, `brief` and `goto` have none.

CardPage.description: An html file the worker wrote, at its first write (epoch ms), and whether the worker showed it.

CardSent.description: A message the worker sent another Claude session, with the callsign of the worker that received it.

Unresumable.description: Why a past worker can't be resumed where it ran: its cwd is no longer one of its floor's folders (`outside`: the floor's dirs moved, or it left the config), or it is a worktree whose folder is gone (`gone`: removed, or deleted).

prompt.description: The user's latest prompt in this session, and Claude's latest answer to the main loop.

CardConversation.description: `promptBy`: the hirer whose prompt its latest is, while that is still the prompt the worker was hired on; else the prompt is the user's.

items.description: The verb's input, the fields the board knows: `tower api <verb>` describes it.
The verb's input, the fields the board knows: `tower api <verb>` describes it.

ConversationAction.description: A verb offered now, with its call when it has one: `drive`, `brief` and `goto` have none.

SessionLink.description: A session a conversation came from or went on to, with when it started.

SessionRef.description: A session by id, with the callsign of the worker it ran as.

CardRun.description: The run a worker is, through every resume: its policy, number, slot (`null` by hand), how it started and its check.

CheckResult.description: A check's run at a slot: its exit code (0, there is work; 1, none; absent when it timed out or never started, `error` saying which), how long it took, its stdout when it found work (at most 2,048 characters) and the end of its stderr when it failed (at most 500).

Seat.description: Where a worker sits on its floor: a workstation of its own, numbered from the landing, or beside the worker it reports to by its crew edge (that worker's card id).

CardVerb.description: `drive` opens the terminal; `submit` sends the worker a prompt from outside its terminal; `goto` goes to the session that resumed the conversation; `review` starts a reviewer of its work in a fork of its checkout; `send-home` ends the worker and every worker under it that runs (`crewOf`), alone when nobody runs under it; `let-go` takes a stranded worker off duty, its conversation left resumable; `carry-on` resumes a worker the host cut off mid-turn on a prompt telling it so; `note` adds a note to the review thread about its work (`NoteVerb`).

CardAction.description: A verb offered now, with its call when it has one: `drive`, `brief` and `goto` have none.

FloorCollection.description: A floor's collection. `by`: the capability of the extension that declares it, on a floor where that extension is on; none when only the config declares it there (decision `extensions`). `owner`: the capability that alone writes it, an extension's: the generic writes are refused there. `doors`: how others list, read, create, edit and delete its items, as its extension declares them, each a verb or read, or why the domain has none.

Door.description: How others reach a store: a verb or read qualified by its capability, or why the domain has no such act.

x.description: The part of the extension that declares its collection, as its item fold made it.

FloorItem.description: `tag`: what the item is called on screen and by workers (`tagOf`).

KeptBy.description: The worker that kept an item (`tower keep`), in the conversation it was in. An item made any other way has none.

sessions.description: The workers on duty and the shells whose cwd is inside any of its paths.

FloorWorktreeRepo.description: `atRisk`: work only this repo's worktree holds; its `risk` names it.

Carried.description: A branch landed as copies: `commits` of it are in its base, `edited` of them a different patch from the branch's.

WorktreeState.description: `carried`: clean, its work landed only as copies, some edited (`isCarried`): removed by its own `remove`, never by Tidy.

WorktreeVerb.description: `recut` restores a lost worktree's folders from its branch, `prune` forgets them; `remove` is offered only when nothing would be lost, or its work landed as copies (`carried`); `discard` throws away work that never landed, its tips named on the checkout's review thread first.

WorktreeCalls.description: `discard` carries what each repo held as shown, refused once it moved; it takes the author of its note.

WorktreeAction.description: A verb offered now, with its call when it has one: `drive`, `brief` and `goto` have none.

absorbed.description: Absorbed in every repo that has it: deleting it loses nothing.

carried.description: Not absorbed, but absorbed or carried in every repo that has it: deleted by its own `delete`, never by Tidy.

BranchVerb.description: `delete` is offered only on a branch absorbed into its base, or carried there as copies.

BranchAction.description: A verb offered now, with its call when it has one: `drive`, `brief` and `goto` have none.

state.description: Where its checkout's work stands: a note is offered only while it is live.

FloorThread.description: A checkout's thread as `floor.threads` holds it: `messages` it holds and the `last` one, `landed` once Tidy files it, where its work stands, and `note` while it is live.

NoteVerb.description: `note` adds a note to a checkout's review thread, offered while its work goes on (`CheckoutState` live): a note on work that landed, or whose worktree is gone, reaches nobody. The API still takes one there.

items.description: The verb's input, the fields the board knows: `tower api <verb>` describes it.
The verb's input, the fields the board knows: `tower api <verb>` describes it.

NoteAction.description: A verb offered now, with its call when it has one: `drive`, `brief` and `goto` have none.

MainCheckouts.description: The main checkouts as git reads them across a floor's repos: unlanded files (`dirty`, tracked or not) and commits `ahead` of their upstreams, summed, and whether a worker on duty runs there.

PolicyView.description: A policy on its floor: valid, with its `header`, `rule` and `next`, or invalid, with its `problems`. `rule`: its crons in words; `next`: its next slot (epoch ms); `approved`: the approval of its current hash; `live`: the current cards of its runs that run; `last`: its latest run, `n` its number; `passed`: its latest pass, for why; `seen`: the newest slot any of its facts names; `offer`: its open offer; `needs`: an `auto` policy that lost the right to run on its own (edited since its approval, or invalid once approved), else a slot held while it is still open (`HeldBy`). `actions`: `run` it now, by hand, and `approve` its current hash, each with its call; `calls` says the same.

check.description: A shell line run at the slot from the floor's hub: exit 0, there is work; 1, none; anything else, it failed.

start.description: `ask`: each slot is offered. `auto`: started while the file's current hash has an approval, offered otherwise.

live.description: The most runs of this policy whose workers run at once; a slot due while full is held.

runner.description: The runner that acts on it; the tower's acts on the policies that name none.

x.description: Each runner's own attributes, under its name.

PolicyHeader.description: A policy's header, its defaults filled in.

CronWhen.description: Slots as crons: the union of theirs, read in `tz` (an IANA zone), else in the tower machine's zone.

Hire.description: Where a run's worker starts and on what model: the spawn verb's own fields (`SPAWN_FIELDS`), which its schema picks.

HeldBy.description: A run that holds a slot: its number, its worker (as it is now) and when it started (epoch ms).

PolicyAction.description: A verb offered now, with its call when it has one: `drive`, `brief` and `goto` have none.

Outcome.description: Why the runner passed a slot: offered it, the check found no work, live was full, or the check failed.

Problem.description: What makes a file no policy, at its path as `tower config check` prints one: `when.cron[1]`, `header`, `prose`.

GalleryShowing.description: A showing in a floor's gallery: what was shown, under the worker that carries it now.

threads.deprecated: since 1.94: the reviews extension's tidy entries, by key, copied here until 2.0.

TidyPlan.description: A floor's Tidy, as listed: the removable worktrees and absorbed kept branches by name, the processes and workers to end (`prunable`), and the logs to archive (`oldLogs`): the floor's sessions', and the closed months (`oldStreams`) of the floor's own streams and of the system's, which every floor's Tidy lists. What extensions would tidy is in `board.adds['floor:<project>'].tidy`.

Prune.description: `reap`: a process whose session no longer runs, orphaned or not. `kill`: a hired worker done with its purpose, quiet since `since` (epoch ms); it can be resumed, but its next turn reads the whole conversation again, uncached.

OldLog.description: A plain log Tidy would archive, by session id, with its size on disk.

OldStream.description: A plain month file Tidy would archive.

FloorVerb.description: `spawn` starts a session, `cut` one in a new worktree of every dir, `shell` a shell in one of the floor's dirs, `editor` opens a dir in the user's editor, `tidy` applies the floor's `TidyPlan` as listed: worktrees and kept branches, landed review threads, leftover processes and idle workers.

FloorCalls.description: `spawn` and `shell` take the directory the user picks, `editor` too; `cut` takes the name, branch and base the user picks, or none.

FloorAction.description: A verb offered now, with its call when it has one: `drive`, `brief` and `goto` have none.

ShelfEntry.description: Something kept on a project's shelf, to read or use beside its sessions: a page the project builds (`html`), a set of markdown files (`md`, a glob, in name order or `desc`), a web page shown in place (`url`), such as a local server's UI, or one opened in a new tab (`link`), for pages that refuse to be framed, such as claude.ai artifacts, a declared renderer framed as a page (`renderer`, its name), or an item of one of the project's collections (`item`, `<collection>/<id>`, the id its file name): a markdown item is read like an `md` entry's file, any other is framed like an `html` entry's page, alone. Paths are relative to the project's hub.

Wait.description: One wait of one worker. `key` (`id@since`) names this wait alone: the worker's next wait has another, so a renderer keys what it does about a wait (a notification, a dismissal, a visit) on it. `since`: epoch ms, the card's `enteredAt`. `detail`: the screen that blocks it, or the tool it asks to run, when known.

WaitReason.description: Why a worker waits on you: `blocked` by a screen, `asks` a question, or holds an outcome nobody has typed to since, `failed` or `done`.

Offer.description: A slot offered and not yet taken, open until the policy's next slot. `key`: `policy@slot`. `check`: what the check found, which the run accepting it records.

items.description: The verb's input, the fields the board knows: `tower api <verb>` describes it.
The verb's input, the fields the board knows: `tower api <verb>` describes it.

OfferAction.description: A verb offered now, with its call when it has one: `drive`, `brief` and `goto` have none.

ProbeVerb.description: A probe offers `run`, a read now, unless it is off: the tower refuses it while a read is in flight or within the floor.

items.description: The verb's input, the fields the board knows: `tower api <verb>` describes it.
The verb's input, the fields the board knows: `tower api <verb>` describes it.

ProbeAction.description: A verb offered now, with its call when it has one: `drive`, `brief` and `goto` have none.

ProbeState.description: A probe's state as `board.probes` says it; the field holds none while the quota extension doesn't run, `off` among it.

ExtraUsage.description: Extra usage: credits spent past the plan's limits, up to a monthly limit, in `currency` units, as read `at` (epoch ms). `reached`: the monthly limit is spent.

verbs.description: Its manifest's verbs, by qualified name.

commands.description: Its manifest's client commands, by name: what renderers that import modules run.

spawn.description: What it adds to the spawn form, when it adds anything.

ExtensionView.description: An extension as the board shows it. `id` names the implementation, `provides` the capability every outward name is qualified by. `off`: the floors it is off on, set there or because a capability it requires is. `problems`: newest first.

ExtensionState.description: `started`; `refused` at load (its manifest, its versions, its dependencies); `failed` at start; `skipped` because something it requires doesn't run; `off` in the config; `restarting` while it is restarted, its calls unavailable.

subject.description: The subject a fold failed on, by its key: `card:<id>`.

ExtensionProblem.description: Why an extension, or a part of it, doesn't run as declared. `error`s keep it from starting, or failed a call; `warn`s leave it running; `info` says how it runs (without an extension it wants). `at`: epoch ms, when it was last found. `count`: how many times. `path`: where in the manifest, `settings.every`.

ProblemLane.description: Where a problem arose: reading the manifests, starting an extension, halting it, a call of a verb or a read, a fold, a link of a chain it wraps, an answer to a hook, a slot or the board trigger, a launch it contributed to.

ExtensionVerb.description: One of an extension's verbs as the board shows it: its qualified name, scope and words.

Scope.description: `system`: a verb or read of the whole system; `project`: one floor's, refused on a floor where its capability is off.

Words.description: A name in words, as a menu or the CLI offers it.

Deprecated.description: A name on its way out: since its provider's version `since`, with what to `use` instead, qualified, and `why`.

ExtensionCommand.description: One of an extension's client commands as the board shows it: the export of a module served at `/x/<cap>/<module>`, and `on`, the subject kinds every subject of which is offered it.

ExtensionSlot.description: One of an extension's slots as the board shows it: `/slots.js` says its rule in words and finds its next slot.

When.description: A rule naming slots: crons, or a period.

EveryWhen.description: Slots as a period, `30s`, `5m` or `2h`, aligned to the UTC clock: `5m` is each multiple of 5 minutes since the epoch.

SpawnFieldView.description: A spawn field the form draws, by name: its value goes in a spawn's `x.<cap>.<name>`. `options`: where its choices are, a path into the extension's own floor part (`floor.x.roles.options`), each `{value, label, hint?}`; without one, it is typed.

Adds.description: What extensions added to one subject, in fold order. `lines`: what `tower whoami` prints for a card's worker. `slots`: a floor's or the board's, which the tower's slot loop fires through each one's `slots['*']`.

BoardAsk.description: An ask as the board carries it: its `key` qualified by its capability, `<cap>:<key>`, and its actions tagged.

Today.description: Today so far, as the board carries it: spend, agent-hours and the waits answered since `since`, the local day's start (epoch ms), and the weekly budget.

outside.description: Points of the week used outside the tower (claude.ai, the desktop app, another machine): `outsideUse`.

usdPerPercent.description: What 1% buys, from the climb less `outside`.

WeeklyBudget.description: The weekly limit as a budget: over the window it is in now, from its first reading (`since`) to the latest where its percent moved, what was spent and how far the percent climbed for it, so what 1% buys and what the percent left buys at that rate. The rate is unknown until the percent has climbed for the tower's spend.

Pace.description: Whether the day's spending lasts: `perDay`, the even daily spend that spends what is left exactly at the reset (all of it in the reset's last day), and `runsOutAt` (epoch ms), when what is left runs out at today's rate, only when that is before the reset.

ClaudeDefaults.description: What Claude runs a new worker on when the launch asks for no model or effort, as observed: settings files, env, plan and `/model` decide it. One value for the machine, as a `/model` pick is saved in the user's settings: a project whose own settings pin a model is not told apart. Absent until a session shows it.

BoardError.description: Why a renderer has no live board: the tower can't build it, `config` until the user fixes the config, `internal` for a failure of its own; or `disconnected`, told by `/tower.js` (never by the tower) while the tower doesn't answer.
